links.outcome: Sensitivity and missed moderate/severe DR after local referral threshold retuning
links.effect: Greifswald-modified RetCAD sensitivity for more-than-mild DR 93.63% vs 70.41% unmodified (diagnosable); specificity fell to 66.5%; missed severe DR 2 vs 13, moderate 13 vs 67. Threshold derived and evaluated on the same local data.
links.quote: Under this scenario, 2 severe DR cases and 13 moderate DR cases would be missed compared to 13 severe DR and 67 moderate DR cases with unmodified RetCAD screening.

links.outcome: Real-world local sensitivity versus pivotal trial performance
links.effect: IDx-DR sensitivity for more-than-mild DR 90.2% in diagnosable patients but 52.7% across all patients, versus 87.2% in the pivotal trial; 25.5% of patients rejected for image quality.
links.quote: The sensitivity for more than mild DR on this data set was 87.2%, which is comparable to our result of diagnosable patients (90.2%), but not for all patients in our study (52.7%) (Abràmoff et al., 2018 ).

links.outcome: Local screening sensitivity including patients without analysable images
links.effect: IDx-DR sensitivity for more than mild DR was 90.2% among diagnosable patients but 52.7% across all local patients; its initial evaluation reported 87.2%.
links.quote: The sensitivity for more than mild DR on this data set was 87.2%, which is comparable to our result of diagnosable patients (90.2%), but not for all patients in our study (52.7%) (Abràmoff et al., 2018 ).

links.outcome: Missed diabetic retinopathy after locally customized referral thresholds
links.effect: In the hypothetical screening scenario, missed severe DR decreased from 13 to 2 cases and missed moderate DR from 67 to 13; all-patient specificity decreased from 90.38% to 66.5%.
links.quote: Under this scenario, 2 severe DR cases and 13 moderate DR cases would be missed compared to 13 severe DR and 67 moderate DR cases with unmodified RetCAD screening.

links.outcome: Diagnostic sensitivity against ophthalmologists' dilated funduscopic examination
links.effect: Unmodified RetCAD sensitivity was 70.41% for more than mild DR and 62.86% for severe DR among analysable images, including images recommended for rejection.
links.quote: The diagnostic sensitivity of the RetCAD algorithm for detecting more than mild DR on analysable images (including the ones recommended to be rejected) was 70.41%, and the sensitivity for severe DR was 62.86%.

links.effect: locally adjusting the threshold increased sensitivity to 93.63% in diagnosable images and 79.87% overall
links.quote: Among the algorithms compared, the RetCAD algorithm with the Greifswald modification demonstrated the highest sensitivity. It achieved a sensitivity of 93.63% for detecting ‘more than mild’ diabetic retinopathy (DR) in diagnosable images, and 79.87% sensitivity across the entire patient population.

links.effect: performance was substantially lower in real-world settings when missing or non-analysable images were included
links.quote: Real-world DR screening performance of AI algorithms, when including non-analysable patients, can be substantially lower than in controlled studies.
